title: Manufacturing Of Robust Natural Fiber Preforms Utilizing Bacterial Cellulose as Binder
protocol: Determine the wet-to-dry mass ratio of bacterial cellulose (BC).
Measure the wet mass of BC, then vacuum dry overnight at 80 °C to measure the dry mass.
Cut a wet BC pellicle equivalent to 18 g of dry BC into small pieces (~1-2 cm).
Soak the cut BC pellicles in 1 L of water for hydration.
Feed the hydrated BC pellicles into a blender with an appropriate amount of water and blend for 2 min.
Pour the blended BC into a 15 L container, adding water until the total volume is 14 L to achieve a concentration of 0.1 g/ml.
Cut 72 g of loose sisal fibers into 1-2 cm lengths.
Add the cut sisal fibers to the BC suspension and stir gently to ensure homogenous dispersion.
Soak the sisal fibers in this suspension overnight.
Open sheet mold and close drainage valve.
Fill the system with deionized (DI) water until the water level reaches the backing wire.
Place a 100 mesh metal forming wire on the backing wire, centered within the sheet mold base.
Close and latch the sheet mold.
Add fresh water until the forming wire is submerged in water.
Pour the prepared sisal fiber-BC suspension into the sheet mold.
Gently stir the suspension to ensure homogeneous distribution of sisal fibers throughout the mold.
Open the drain valve to allow water drainage, forming a wet filter cake on the forming wire.
Remove the forming wire from the sheet mold and place it on blotting paper.
Place additional blotting papers and a metal plate on top of the filter cake.
Flip the filter cake around with the forming wire facing the top.
Remove the forming wire and place fresh blotting paper directly on top of the filter cake, followed by a metal plate.
Place a 10 kg weight on top of the metal plate to press water out of the filter cake.
Replace soaked blotting papers with fresh ones when fully saturated.
Press the filter cake again using a weight of 10 kg.
Perform a final pressing of 1 ton in a hot press to consolidate the fiber preform.
Heat the hot press up to 120 °C.
Allow approximately 4 hours for heating.
Reduce the temperature of the hot press to room temperature (RT).
Allow the preform to cool down prior to removal from the hot press.
Cut a 2 × 2 cm² BC-sisal fiber preform.
Stick the cut preform onto SEM stub using carbon tabs.
Coat the sample in a Cr sputter coater operating at 75 mA for 1 min.
Image the BC-sisal fiber preform with field emission gun SEM in in-lens mode using a beam energy of 5 kV.
Place the preform on top of the tooling side, which consists of a non-porous PTFE coated glass release fabric.
Cover the preform with a porous PTFE coated glass release fabric (peel ply).
Cover the peel ply with a porous flow medium.
Position the omega tubes at the intended resin inlet and outlet of the VARI set up.
Place the omega tubes on top of the porous flow medium.
Ensure that the length of the omega tubes is as wide as the flow medium.
Insert pressure sensitive tapes around the periphery of the set up.
Leave the paper backing of the pressure sensitive tapes in place.
Insert the resin feed and outlet tubes into the openings of the omega tubes.
Cover the set up with a fluoroethylene polymer based bagging film.
Seal the bag using pressure sensitive tapes.
Seal the resin feed tube.
Position the other end of the resin outlet tube on top of the breather cloth.
Place a metal plate on top of the inner bag where the fiber preform is.
Add a piece of breather cloth over the metal plate.
Identify the position for the through bag vacuum valve and place the bottom piece on the breather cloth.
Place the vacuum sealant tape around the internal bag.
Position a vacuum bagging film on top of the internal bag.
Seal the vacuum bagging film to form pleats.
Insert the sealant tape inside the pleat to complete the seal.
Cut a small 'x' on the vacuum bagging film where the bottom piece of the valve is.
Screw in the top piece to complete the through bag vacuum valve.
Check for vacuum leaks after connecting the quick connect fitting and pulling a vacuum.
Prepare the resin by mixing the epoxy and hardener at a weight ratio of 100 to 19.
Degas the resin at reduced pressure to remove air bubbles.
Feed the resin via tubing connected to the omega tube slowly into the fiber preform.
Allow the resin to flow out from the resin outlet tube and soak into the breather cloth until no air bubbles are observed.
Seal the outlet tube once the resin has impregnated adequately.
Allow the resin to cure for 24 hours at room temperature.
Post-cure the sample at 50 °C for 16 hours.
